items.claim: set-overlays only takes debug features
A root removed while its canvas stays mounted keeps the panel's override
The page accepts `yo` and requests from any frame
items.note: A message whose `source` is a different window is ignored. A null `source` still passes, because jsdom sets none; every real sender (another frame, or the content script) has a non-null one.

items.claim: An emptied override still forces the overlay on
items.note: This also changes core: `withOverride` now leaves an overlay that is off, off, when the override turns nothing on.

items.claim: The root keeps the trace and coords rings it first saw while its getters read the current dep
items.note: The root holds a ring that follows the canvas's current one: it moves watches, subscribers and cursors over, and rebinds on a dep-registry change. The coords ring is stable once the inspection dep has made it, so only reads rebind it.

items.claim: `dimension` is decided once, from the first root node, so an empty 3D canvas shows as 2d
items.note: A canvas with a `camera3d` dep is 3d. A session's notices send `root-added` again when a root's label or dimension changes, and `client.ts` keeps a re-announced root in its place in the list.

items.claim: `connect` keeps listening after `bye`
`serialize` writes Error, RegExp, DataView, DOM nodes and other built-ins as `{}`
items.note: Each now gets `$class`, and errors, regexps and buffers also get their own fields. Maps and sets are recognized by their internal slot, so an object whose `toStringTag` only claims `Map` no longer throws.

items.claim: The history ring is not reset when the scene is swapped
items.note: Each scene gets a fresh ring behind the same follower.

items.claim: A root's removal never drops the panel's override: `dropOverride` looks the root up after the hook already deleted it
A root's `dimension` is fixed at registration from the scene's first root, so a 3D canvas mounted empty is reported as 2D for good
The window hook accepts a `yo` and requests from any frame, so an embedded iframe can take over the panel's session and steer the canvas
Clearing everything the panel laid over a canvas leaves an empty override in force, turning the debug overlay on for a canvas whose own `debug` is off
`get-history`'s position answers index/total from the scene stack but canUndo/canRedo from an open journal
The trace and coord rings are captured once per follow/attach, so a dispatch trace replaced mid-session is never watched
After `bye`, `connect`'s transport listener stays subscribed and the session can never be reopened over that transport
`set-overlays` accepts any key, so a posted `{ highlight: true }` reaches the debug sink as a non-array and throws
A request whose handler throws a non-Error is never answered, and the panel's promise hangs forever
The history ring keeps the previous scene's steps after the canvas swaps scenes
`get-registry` reports `shortcut: null` for an action whose key binding gives it a shortcut, while tools report their live keys
`serialize` writes an Error, a RegExp or a boxed primitive as an empty `{}`, against its own contract, and a throwing `ownKeys` fails the whole request
